status: Pre-edit receiver/operation trace; source evidence, not execution.

evidence: SignedLength::from_metres rejects only nonfinite leaves; finite extreme signed values are admitted.
InverseKinematicsConfig retains signed clearances and sole_contact_margin_metres as SignedLength; TacticalCombatConfig::validate has no narrower bounds for these fields.

FootClearanceFloor::apply computes the complete surface+sole+clearance sum, then uses max with target.y before checked_foot_target; ordinary_terrain_target similarly takes max of its complete floor before checking the final target.
In contrast, terrain_minimum_ankle_y and transition_minimum_ankle_y admit their complete computed floor before flight_projection takes max with target.y.
completed_floor_invariant.inference: IEEE f32 overflow or cancellation involving nonfinite intermediates can leave a nonfinite completed floor, which max may hide behind a finite target. This is a static arithmetic-contract finding, not a reproduced runtime incident.
completed_floor_invariant.decision: Admit/check the complete floor before applying target.max in both direct floor paths. Use the existing owning AnimationValueError::Overflow and floor aggregate. This intentionally repairs rejection of invalid completed arithmetic; do not describe it as solely a representation-preserving refactor.
completed_floor_invariant.preservation: Preserve surface+sole+clearance and height+sole-margin expression order, final lerp/max order for finite inputs, signed/zero floor values and the existing return/error channel. Do not check individual sole/toe constituents before their complete existing sole-first/toe-second maximum. Do not add clamps, arbitrary lower bounds or zero fallbacks.
completed_floor_invariant.coverage_limit: Existing tests can be adapted; no new extreme-input case/assertion is authorized. No local numerical or runtime probe was run.

normal_fixture_decision.evidence: Only two production forwarders pass terrain normals into slope_aligned_world_rotation. Its complete body is normalization, angle/arc/quaternion math and returns the final native rotation; it does not forward to another application query or retain an untyped normal. The existing steep-normal fixture calls this kernel twice with one Vec3::normalize output and has two assertions.
locked_dependency_evidence: bevy_math 0.19.1 direction.rs:563-564 delegates Dir3::new to new_and_length; lines 587-596 compute a finite-positive length and component division value/length.

glam 0.32.1 f32/vec3.rs:626-630 Vec3::normalize multiplies by length_recip; lines 641-647 try_normalize similarly multiply by a checked reciprocal. Lines 1422-1428 scalar division performs per-component division.

Consequently replacing the original fixture normalization with Dir3::new is not proven bit-identical, and wrapping its already-normalized output would introduce an extra normalization. The earlier planning statement that checked admission on the raw vector simply preserves the same two normalizations was insufficient.
normal_fixture_decision.decision: Keep Dir3 through the application alignment forwarders. Project its native vector exactly at their call to the existing complete slope_aligned_world_rotation numerical kernel. Keep that kernel input native and its original try_normalize/arithmetic unchanged; it is a verified numeric endpoint, not a private application forwarder. This preserves all production vector bits and leaves the existing raw numerical-kernel fixture and both assertions unchanged, without an unchecked constructor or extra normalization.
normal_fixture_decision.scope_limit: This native-kernel classification does not permit a raw-normal field/parameter in the outer alignment forwarders or another application helper. Document the world normal/local sole-axis handoff at the actual numerical owner as needed.
